items.title: Mozambique: President Chapo heads to Antalya for COP31 climate summit
items.summary: Mozambican President Daniel Francisco Chapo will attend the World Climate Action Summit from 11 to 12 November, as part of the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31), taking place in Antalya, Republic of Türkiye, under the theme “Towards a Sustainable, Resilient and Equitable Future” During his stay in the country, the Head of State will also take part in several high-level meetings and events dedicated to the climate agenda, providing opportunities for dialogue and coordination on global challenges and responses to climate change Mozambique’s participation in the Summit aims to reaffirm the country’s commitment to global climate action and mobilise international cooperation to address the impacts of climate change, with particular attention to the need to strengthen climate finance for the most vulnerable countries The President will be accompanied on the visit by the First Lady, Gueta Chapo; the Minister in the Presidency for Civil Affairs, Ricardo Sengo; the Secretary of State for Land and Environment, Gustavo Dgedge…

items.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket fridge hacking
items.summary: Fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets across France were affected last month France has accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of being behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers across the country last month Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the attack was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression", adding those who were responsible would be hit with sanctions Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless The French hacking, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food in France was followed by a similar attack against supermarkets across several other European countries.

items.title: Republican Thomas Massie seeks to force House vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over Iran war
items.summary: Trump critic Thomas Massie is calling for a vote to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, accusing Hegseth of waging war without congressional approval Republican lawmaker Thomas Massie, an outspoken critic of President Donald Trump , introduced eight articles of impeachment against US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday as pressure builds on the Trump administration over the Iran war The resolution proposed by the Kentucky congressman accuses Hegseth of conducting the war illegally without congressional authorization. Massie also claims Hegseth has abused his powers as the head of the Pentagon Massie is using a special procedure that could see the US House of Representatives vote on the resolution within two days, with the legislative chamber still dominated by Republicans To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Trump defended Hegseth in a telephone interview with the Reuters news agency after the articles were filed "Well, he won two wars.

items.title: 'Devastating message' as ANC records worst-ever result in South Africa election
items.summary: Voters cast their ballots at a polling station during South Africa's local government elections in Johannesburg South Africa's ANC has recorded its worst-ever showing in local elections since Nelson Mandela led the country out of apartheid and into democracy more than 30 years ago, a result the party has called "catastrophic" While it won the most votes of all parties in the country, the African National Congress won 31% of the overall vote, one third down from the 46% it gained in 2021, and a far cry from the 65% 20 years ago The story of its decline is also clear in the provinces and cities. The party won a majority in just one of the country's nine provinces, Limpopo. In 2021 it won six. It also won the most votes in just two of the eight cities, compared with six at the last local elections The Democratic Alliance (DA) came second in the overall vote with 25%, retaining majority control of the city of Cape Town.
